_readme: Detection patterns a RAG recon scan trips, derived from the traffic
This is not a generic prompt-attack list. Every category below was
written by reading a captured scan back and asking which of our own
queries a defender's prompt monitoring would pick out. That is why
there is no injection or credential-hunting category among the
scanner's own patterns: ragmap is read-only and sends nothing of that
shape. The two categories that do cover such text are marked
operator_supplied, because the only way such a string reaches the
wire is if someone passed it in --topic, --rare-token or
A trigger is a pattern where * matches anything and literal fragments
match on word boundaries, so 'token' does not fire inside
burst is the number of matches inside one minute that makes a pattern
count. One 'what does the document say about X' is a user; twenty in
a minute is a sweep, and only the second is worth reporting.
Extend or replace with --opsec-rules FILE. A category of the same name
merges its triggers; a new name is added.

corpus_enumeration.description: Asking the assistant to list its own documents or subjects
corpus_enumeration.advice: ragmap opens discovery this way on purpose, because a target that answers has already given up the corpus map. Where quiet matters more, supply --topic, --second-topic, --absent-topic and --rare-token yourself: discovery is then skipped entirely. A few such queries remain either way, because shape detection has to ask something before anything is known.

document_sweep.description: The same framing repeated across many subjects
document_sweep.advice: This is the shape of topic confirmation and of every retrieval measurement after it, so it cannot be removed - only spread out. Raise --delay and --jitter, or drop a tier with --spend.
triggers: what does the document say about *
what do your documents say about *

verbatim_extraction.description: Asking for source text reproduced word for word
verbatim_extraction.advice: Unavoidable for the verbatim-leak check, which exists to prove that hiding citations does not hide the corpus. Drop it with --skip generation.verbatim where the finding is not worth the noise.

context_expansion.description: Pulling more of a passage than the answer offered
context_expansion.advice: Ask a separate question about a neighbouring subject instead; adjacent passages come back on their own.

malformed_input.description: Deliberately broken requests, used to read error handling
malformed_input.advice: Error-verbosity probing is a handful of requests but it is the loudest thing in the scan per request, and it often lands in a different log than chat traffic. --skip errors.verbosity removes it.

off_domain_control.description: General-knowledge questions put to a corpus assistant
off_domain_control.advice: These are the control queries that make routing and thresholds measurable. They look like a confused user rather than an attacker, which is usually the quietest thing in the scan.

identifier_lookup.description: A bare internal identifier sent as the whole query
identifier_lookup.advice: A single rare literal is how lexical and dense retrieval are told apart; there is no softer form of it. It is one request.

operator_secrets.advice: ragmap never generates this. It reached the wire through --topic, --rare-token or --seed-queries, and it moves the engagement from reconnaissance to something needing its own authorisation.

operator_injection.description: Operator-supplied text shaped like prompt injection
operator_injection.advice: ragmap is read-only and sends nothing of this shape. A match means text you supplied would be logged as an attack attempt against your client.
